bluf: ICEA is a Poznań, Poland digital agency founded 2007 that sells SEO as its flagship, with AI Search, paid campaigns and CRO around it, to SMB ecommerce sellers, leading with volume claims: 3,320 satisfied clients and 7,000+ campaigns across 17 years. The record shows a house that contradicts two of the lines it sells: it publishes no llms.txt while selling AI visibility and runs no testing tool while selling CRO. The one thing a rival should know: the Horus read is Neutral at -7.1 and most exposed to KJ4, and with displacement 69.9 on the Monsoon read it is very likely that its SMB book buys on price.
doing:
ICEA positions itself as a Polish digital agency with global reach serving ecommerce as a one stop shop, SEO, paid campaigns and CRO backed by in house R&D tools: in plain words, a Polish SEO shop that added media and UX so a store need not go elsewhere. Its headline claim is scale: 3,320 satisfied clients, 7,000+ campaigns and 10,000+ SEO consultations across 17 years, plus 30% of clients by referral, 3% churn and 237 partner firms, all quoted as claims.

The mix is twelve services: general, shop and local SEO, an SEO audit, AI Search, Google, Meta, TikTok, Amazon and Allegro Ads, programmatic and UX. SEO leads at a score of 3: the title leads with SEO agency and the homepage calls SEO its flagship, delivered for 17 years. Three core lines score 2. AI Search / GEO rests on a dedicated AI Search page citing its own CTR research and a Botland case tracking growth in AI Overview visibility. CRO rests on UX in the title and nav and a kotarbau.pl case pairing SEO with a UX mega menu redesign. Paid Search rests on Google Ads in the title and a Digital Ads menu that includes Bing. Retail Media, Paid Social, Programmatic & CTV and Local score 1 each. The one proprietary asset is widocznosc.ai, an AI visibility sub organisation in its JSON-LD; no partner is listed.

Its AI posture is AI Search sold for AI Overviews and generative answers, backed by its own CTR research; AI Automation / Agents scores 0.

The record lists no dated moves, no news and no jobs, and no pricing signal at all, so the pricing model is unknown. Absent for an agency claiming this volume: Content & Digital PR, Data & Measurement, Email & CRM and Web & Product all score 0, no partner badge is shown, and only 5 clients are named against a claim of 3,320.
clients:
The record marks its client type as SMB and lists ten verticals: home and garden, children's products, health and beauty, sport and recreation, fashion, books and media, FMCG, electronics and appliances, automotive and education. The home market is Poland, with Poznań the only office listed.

The book holds 5 clients, 2 with observed needs and 3 names only. Organic demand is the top need with 2 clients and web build and platform follows with 1. The observed names are Botland (a case study on squeezing more from SEO, organic demand) and kotarbau.pl (a case study on SEO meeting UX in a new mega menu, organic demand plus web build and platform). The names only are czesci-moto.pl (organic visibility growth in automotive), sklepdrapieznik.pl (a migration and visibility growth) and Inspiro Online (reaching the top 3 in Google), slugs that point at organic demand without the record coding it, so the need is inferred from the SEO line it leads with. All 5 are Polish online stores, which fits the ecommerce positioning.

No client on record sits on another tracked agency's book.

The read is most exposed to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer), driven by Paid Search and Paid Social, and to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that the Google Ads, Meta Ads and Allegro Ads hours these stores buy are the first absorbed by platform automation, and that what they need next is the feed, entity and first party data layer the record shows ICEA does not offer. The tailwinds are KJ2 and KJ1, and the Botland case on AI Overview visibility is the one piece of evidence it can sell either.
house: The record marks 1 of 3 scored say and do lines practised and house integrity at 33.3. AI Search / GEO is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt while its sitemap holds 6 AI topic URLs. CRO is contradicted: it sells CRO and no testing tool was detected on its own homepage. Both are listed as gaps. Paid Search is unknown because the Transparency Center lookup was blocked, and publishing cadence is corroborated by 5 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 25 in 365 out of 835. No AI crawlers are blocked. The tag stack is gtm and cookiebot on WordPress, with no social pixel, test tool or ABM stack detected. Google's ad transparency status is blocked. LinkedIn's ad library returned not found: 64 ads match the name query and the near name advertiser ICEA LION Group (19) was excluded, leaving 0 company ads. No Meta or TikTok check is recorded.
market:
The Horus read puts ICEA at a tailwind index of -7.1, band Neutral. It is best placed for KJ2 at net 0.269, driven by Paid Search and AI Search / GEO, and for KJ1 at 0.202; it is most exposed to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) at -0.337, driven by Paid Search and Paid Social, and to KJ6 at -0.312. The best scenario fit is The Toll Road at 42/100. It is partial on P1 (audited AI visibility) and P4 (automation inputs); P2, P3, P6, P7 and P8 are absent; P5 unknown.

The Monsoon read is 62.4, band Onshore wind, migration 54.9 against displacement 69.9, observed: the Poznań hub office is a delivery footprint in Eastern Europe, offset by an inferred destination term. 58 of the index is the sold mix, SEO (21) and Paid Search (9) most movable; the shore split is 65% South and Southeast Asia and 26% Eastern Europe, and automation overlaps 21% of the movable hours. It claims onshore delivery in its own words (in house R&D tools) while most hours are movable.
openings:
The strongest opening is price. Displacement 69.9 on an observed Monsoon read, an SMB ecommerce book and a footprint already in Eastern Europe make it very likely, with high confidence, that an offshore delivered rival can undercut its SEO and Google Ads hours line by line. The falsifier is a captured pricing page showing outcome priced tiers, absent from the record.

Two contradictions lead: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt, and it sells CRO with no testing tool on its own homepage, so a rival showing both on its own house can test the in house R&D tools claim in the sales room. P1 is partial with no audited AI visibility product, so an audited AI Overview citation number likely beats a single Botland case.

The judgment exposure is KJ4: Google, Meta and Allegro Ads hours are the ones platform automation removes, and P4 is partial, so an offer built on first party data, creative volume and measurement depth likely wins the paid conversation. P2 is absent, so the feed and entity layer on its shop SEO line is unclaimed, and P5 is unknown, so an outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot have in public.
